notes: Indie dev team (2 full-time) building an AI-first writing assistant for indie authors. Found Redwood from blog post on cost/perf. Primary motivation: predictable per-token costs and simple SDKs. Early tests: embeddings for semantic search + light chat summarization. Latency target is lenient (150-300ms) but UI needs streaming to show incremental drafts. Very cost sensitive — expects sporadic bursty traffic (covering 50-200 monthly heavy users). Quoted on office hours: 'we need streaming in the quickstart so the UI feels alive' and 'pricing needs to scale down for hobbyist authors'. No enterprise security needs; just basic billing + invites. Current blockers: card verification errors and wanting a short example that shows streaming + token usage breakdown. Likely to convert to small paid tier if streaming quickstart and one month of promotional credit are provided. No AE touch yet — growth inbox owns inbound.
use_case_summary: Prototype uses hosted API for three flows: embeddings for doc search across uploaded manuscripts, chat assistant for author Q&A and scene suggestions (light context windows ~2-3k tokens), and summarization for chapter abstracts. Low concurrency, bursty spikes when author community opens new beta. Wants SDK streaming for better UX and clear token/cost visibility in the dashboard.
